Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views

Class ActionResult

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.views.ActionResult
@BeanType(properties="contractVersion,outcome,replay,refusalCode,message,row,resultForm") public class ActionResult extends Object
The typed result a row action's submit returns — the load-bearing half of the write path.

A raw HTML fragment response cannot carry the distinction the consumer's non-optimistic UI rule requires: a row must not show "acknowledged" because a request was sent, only because the remote system was read back and said so. This typed result carries exactly that distinction — an outcome discriminator, the authoritative row data to re-render from, a replay marker, and a refusalCode — so the juneau-views.js runtime can paint what actually happened (success, failure, a named refusal, or an honest unknown) rather than what the request asked for.

Its own, independent contract version

The action-result is a third independently-versioned wire contract, alongside VIEW_META and the FTL card/slot envelope. Its CONTRACT_VERSION is deliberately its own constant and is not aliased to VIEW_META: aliasing a per-view contract's version onto a separate contract couples two unrelated client/server locksteps, so this contract versions itself.

Refusals are an opaque, namespaced code — not a framework-closed enum

A refusal's refusalCode is an opaque namespaced string, not a framework-closed enum and not a free-text message. Refusals span two independent sources, and the framework must be able to render a refusal it has never heard of:

  • Framework transport codes come from BoundaryReason.name() (e.g. CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING), already on the wire as the X-Request-Boundary header and the rejection envelope's reason.
  • Consumer codes are namespaced app: / write-guard: strings for concepts Juneau knows nothing about ("not armed", "arming expired", "confirmation does not match this incident", "a previous attempt's outcome is unknown").

The runtime renders ANY code as a visible named refusal without the framework needing to know consumer concepts exist.

Reserved async terminal outcomes

cancelled and cancelled-after-effect are reserved from day one (as VIEW_META reserved rowActions before it was implemented), even though a synchronous write never emits them. A future async/streaming variant can therefore emit them without a second result-contract bump and a three-sided lockstep.

Example:

// A success carrying the authoritative row read back from the remote system. ActionResult ok = ActionResult.success(incidentReadBack); // A named refusal from the consumer's write gate. ActionResult no = ActionResult.refusal("write-guard:not-armed"); // A recorded prior outcome, labelled as a replay rather than re-calling. ActionResult again = ActionResult.success(incidentReadBack).replay(true);

    • resultForm

      public String resultForm
      The follow-up read-only form-source URL a receipt is painted from; omitted from the wire when unset.
      Honored on success only

      This is the mechanical form of a receipt must never look like a receipt for a write that didn't happen. On a failure, a refusal, an unknown, or a transport failure this field is ignored, no follow-up GET is issued, and nothing is swapped — so no result host can appear for a write that did not commit.

      The served payload must not carry a form

      The URL serves a ModalDef, and that payload must not declare a form. A result host is terminal by definition: the write already committed, so there is nothing left to gate. A payload carrying inputs is refused visibly rather than rendered read-only or silently stripped, because it is a consumer authoring bug and should be visible as one.

      It is a swap, not a new dialog

      The runtime paints the receipt into the dialog that is already open, at the same layer depth, and only when that dialog opted in with ModalDef.keepOpenOnSubmit. Set on a result whose dialog did not opt in, the swap is dropped, the success is reported unchanged, and the runtime emits one non-alarming diagnostic rather than either opening a layer or making a successful write look failed.
